title: Braise
summary: Sear then simmer covered in liquid — transforms tough cuts.
origins: French braiser means "live coals" — classic peasant technique of cooking in a covered pot buried in embers. Every culture has a version: coq au vin, osso buco, Filipino adobo, Mexican birria.
history: Escoffier codified braising in French repertoire; American Dutch oven and slow-cooker adaptations made it weeknight-accessible. Collagen breaks down around 160–180°F over time — the science behind fork-tender pot roast.
teaching: Sear protein first — Maillard flavor survives the long simmer.
Liquid should come halfway up, not cover — you're steaming + bathing.
Low oven (300°F) or stovetop bare simmer — never a rolling boil.
fun_fact: Braising is patience chemistry: collagen needs time above 160°F to become silky gelatin.
